readings.title: The Reign of Jehoahaz of Israel
readings.subtitle: Oppression by Aram
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:1] In the twenty-third year of Yo’ash son of Aḥazyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, Yeho’aḥaz son of Yěhu began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, and reigned seventeen years. [2] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and followed the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin. <dn>He</dn> did not turn away from them. [3] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl, and <dn>He</dn> gave them into the hand of Ḥaza’ěl sovereign of Aram, and into the hand of Ben-Haḏaḏ son of Ḥaza’ěl, all the days. [4] Then Yeho’aḥaz sought <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> listened to him, for <dn>He</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> the oppression of Yisra’ěl, because the sovereign of Aram oppressed them. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Yisra’ěl a saviour, so that they came out from under the hand of Aram. And the children of Yisra’ěl dwelt in their tents as before. [6] However, they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Yaroḇ‛am, who had made Yisra’ěl sin, but walked in them. Moreover, the Ashěrah also remained in Shomeron. [7] For <dn>He</dn> left of the army of Yeho’aḥaz only fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, for the sovereign of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.

readings.title: The Death of Jehoahaz
readings.subtitle: Joash Succeeds Him
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:8] And the rest of the acts of Yeho’aḥaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [9] So Yeho’aḥaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Shomeron. And Yo’ash his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Reign of Jehoash of Israel
readings.subtitle: He Follows in the Sins of Jeroboam
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:10] In the thirty-seventh year of Yo’ash sovereign of Yehuḏah, Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, sixteen years. [11] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>He</dn> did not turn away from all the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin – he walked in it.

readings.title: Hazael Threatens Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Joash of Judah Pays Tribute
readings.text: [2 Kings 12:17] And Ḥaza’ěl sovereign of Aram went up and fought against Gath, and captured it. And Ḥaza’ěl set his face to go up to Yerushalayim. [18] And Yeho’ash sovereign of Yehuḏah took <dn>את</dn> all the set-apart gifts that his fathers, Yehoshaphat and Yehoram and Aḥazyahu, sovereigns of Yehuḏah, had set apart, and <dn>את</dn> his own set-apart gifts, and <dn>את</dn> all the gold found in the treasuries of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in the sovereign’s house, and sent them to Ḥaza’ěl sovereign of Aram. Then he went away from Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Assassination of Joash of Judah
readings.subtitle: Amaziah Succeeds Him
readings.text: [2 Kings 12:19] And the rest of the acts of Yo’ash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [20] And his servants rose up and made a conspiracy, and smote <dn>את</dn> Yo’ash in the house of Millo, which goes down to Silla. [21] For Yozaḵar son of Shim‛ath and Yehozaḇaḏ son of Shoměr, his servants, struck him. So he died, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. And Amatsyah his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Elisha's Final Prophecy
readings.subtitle: The Arrow of Deliverance from Aram
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:14] And Elisha had become sick with the sickness in which he died. And Yo’ash the sovereign of Yisra’ěl came down to him, and wept over his face, and said, “O my father, my father, the chariots of Yisra’ěl and their horsemen!” [15] And Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and some arrows.” And he took a bow and some arrows. [16] And he said to the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, “Place your hand on the bow.” So he placed his hand, and Elisha placed his hands on the hands of the sovereign, [17] and said, “Open the east window.” And he had opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot.” And he shot. Then he said, “The arrow of deliverance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the arrow of deliverance from Aram, for you shall strike <dn>את</dn> Aram at Aphěq until it is finished.” [18] Then he said, “Take the arrows,” and he took them. And he said to the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, “Strike the ground,” and he struck three times, and stopped. [19] And the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> was wroth with him and said, “You should have struck five or six times, then you would have stricken <dn>את</dn> Aram till its utter destruction. But now you shall strike <dn>את</dn> Aram only three times.”

readings.title: The Death and Miracle of Elisha
readings.subtitle: A Dead Man Revived by His Bones
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:20] And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the raiding bands from Mo’aḇ came into the land in the spring of the year. [21] And it came to be, they were burying a man, and there they saw <dn>את</dn> a raiding band, and cast <dn>את</dn> the man in the burial-site of Elisha. And the man fell and touched the bones of Elisha, and came to life and stood on his feet.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Compassion for Israel
readings.subtitle: A Covenant Remembered
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:22] And Ḥaza’ěl sovereign of Aram oppressed <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl all the days of Yeho’aḥaz. [23] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed favour to them, and had compassion on them, and turned toward them, for the sake of <dn>His</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> Aḇraham, <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq, and <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ, and would not destroy them or cast them from <dn>His</dn> presence as yet.

readings.title: Jehoash Recovers Cities from Aram
readings.subtitle: The Prophecy Fulfilled
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:24] And Ḥaza’ěl sovereign of Aram died. And Ben-Haḏaḏ his son reigned in his place. [25] And Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz recovered from the hand of Ben-Haḏaḏ, son of Ḥaza’ěl, <dn>את</dn> the cities which he had taken out of the hand of Yeho’aḥaz his father in battle. Yo’ash struck him three times, and he recovered <dn>את</dn> the cities of Yisra’ěl.
